messages:
lucas: quick brain dump — we keep hitting fragmentation during offload bursts across tenants. proposing a 'soft-evict marker' that tags pages as candidates for cooperative defrag rather than forcible eviction. marker doesn't change residency immediately, just makes page eligible for background compaction.
mina: sounds promising. how do you foresee the marker interacting with per-tenant quotas? we can't let one tenant's defrag hog IO.
lucas: idea: markers carry a weight and owner tag. background compactor consumes budget from a global defrag pool with per-tenant caps. compactor will prefer local (same-tenant) markers first, then best-effort cross-tenant only when headroom exists.
tj: curious about correctness/latency tradeoffs. if a page is marked soft-evict but still in-use, we need a quick way to cancel the operation. can we keep it lock-free?
sophia: +1 on cancel path. maybe marker lifecycle: MARK -> SCHEDULED -> MOVING -> COMPLETED. If a fault/hit occurs, transition to CANCELLED. keep state cheap: 2-bit flag in page metadata and a sequence counter.
evan: also think about multi-GPU scenarios. marker needs to be visible cluster-wide; we can't have stale markers on remote nodes. gossip or a lightweight epoch broadcast?
lucas: proposal: lease-based marker with short TTL (e.g., 200ms). compactor grabs marker by acquiring lease (CAS on marker epoch). lease ensures only one compactor proceeds. renewals allowed if operation long.
mina: can we fold marker into existing residency bits to avoid adding per-page memory? i worry about metadata bloat for small pages.
sophia: suggestion: use a hybrid: for hot pages, use a sidecar bloom/bitmap per arena describing soft-evict set. exact marker only materializes when compactor starts moving page.
tj: that reduces on-page overhead at cost of occasional false positives — acceptable for best-effort defrag.
evan: eviction-bot: defrag job scheduled on node-3, priority=low, budget=40MB/s :gear:
lucas: good to have a throttled streaming mover. another safety: when moving a page, write a tombstone mapping so in-flight requests either wait or get redirected to new location. need to measure worst-case p99 of movement.
mina: do we want user-facing APIs? e.g., runtime hint: prefer-compaction=true for heavy long-lived embeddings workloads.
sophia: yes. add a route in allocation attrs: { compactible: true|false, compact_priority: 0..10 }
lj: (typo) — ignore
tj: edge cases: pinned pages (e.g., pinned for long KV cache) should be excluded. marker should honor pin count > 0.
evan: telemetry: emit marker lifecycle events and compaction latency histograms. correlate with tenant cost buckets so we can tune caps.
lucas: next steps: mockup prototype in arena-sim (single-node) to validate throughput and p99. i'll open an RFC PR with state machine and bitmap prototype.
sophia: can you add a fail-safe: if movement fails after N retries, revert marker and mark page non-compactible for T minutes to avoid hot loops.
lucas: yes — backoff and temporary blacklist per page-range.
mina: ack. please include a test that simulates 3 tenants with skewed allocation patterns.
lucas: will do. ping me if you want to join the RFC review. @sophia @tj @mina
sophia: will review. :thumbsup:
eviction-bot: nightly-compactor-run: scheduled, node-3 queued, estimated-run=02:30:00
